approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local graph genetic algorithm whose oracle budget is spent by a Gaussian-process Thompson sampler. It keeps every molecule scored in the current session in an archive and the best sixty-four in a breeding population, draws breeding parents from high-scoring quantiles, and builds a fresh field of one hundred and sixty de novo offspring for each announced batch of ten by connected-fragment crossover with an optional finishing edit or by a short random walk of atom, bond and ring edits, refusing anything that is not a single ordinary connected graph, is already known, or introduces sulfur environments outside a fixed envelope more often than its own parents did. It then fits a Gaussian process to this session's accepted scores alone, using integer-count radius-two Morgan environments under a generalized Tanimoto kernel with scores recentred and rescaled by their running mean and spread, and draws one correlated posterior sample across the whole field for each of the ten batch positions. The ten molecules sent to the oracle are the sequential maxima of those draws, each winner removed before the next position, so a candidate the model rates poorly on average can still take a position when its sampled residual is large. On top of that the Parent adds one reaction to stagnation: it counts announced batches that fail to raise the session's own best score, and while that count stands at three or more it offers the sampler only the forty members of the field with the highest predicted mean, restoring the full field on the first improving batch. Nothing in it ever checks whether the width of the uncertainty it samples from matches the width of the errors it has actually been making.
approach.novelty: This node changes one number and nothing else: how wide the uncertainty is that the existing sampler draws from. Before each announced batch it looks back at its own recent one-step-ahead predictions - the mean and the uncertainty it published for each molecule in the batch it chose that molecule, against the score the oracle returned - takes the typical size of those errors in units of its own claimed uncertainty, and widens every candidate's uncertainty by that single factor before the sampler reads it. If the model has been honest, or over-cautious, the factor is one and the run is the Parent's exactly, bit for bit. The allocation rule is untouched: the same predicted means, the same random numbers in the same order, the same correlations, the same stall-time eligibility list, the same tie rule. Siblings on this Parent all changed what was on offer or how it was modelled - more distant chemistry, a quota for distant purchases, a structural admission floor, a wider prior far from the archive, a mixture uncertainty model - and every one of them changed the predicted means and so the ordering itself. This is the first arm here that leaves the ordering statistic alone and corrects only the width of the noise around it, measured from the method's own record of being wrong rather than from any fixed constant or any distance assumption.

observed_bottleneck: The number this Parent's allocation rule treats as its uncertainty is not the uncertainty its own predictions actually have, and no arm on this Anchor has ever touched that number. Re-reading n-61b9b3bfb40d's own one-step-ahead records - the predictive mean and SD logged for each selected candidate in the batch it was chosen, against the score it then received - the 4,350 standardized residuals have mean square 31.79 overall, which the round-45 reading splits as 40.72 for picks near the accepted archive against 6.69 far, and the deficit runs in opposite directions by objective: on sitagliptin_mpo the median absolute standardized residual is 3.334 and only 19.2 per cent of picks land within one posterior SD (42.3 per cent fall more than three SDs below prediction), while on median_2 it is 0.257 with 95.6 per cent inside one SD. The inherited correlated Thompson rule consumes exactly that SD: it adds a correlated residual whose per-candidate marginal width is the predictive SD to the predictive mean and takes ten sequentially masked maxima, so a dispersion that is roughly five times too narrow in the bulk on one objective and slightly too wide on another decides which candidate wins each position. Three independent round-45 arms attacked every surrounding layer and none could reach this object: n-907d480bc1fe raised far-field prior variance by archive distance in 435 of 435 batches and improved held-out chemotype coverage, but was gated to exactly zero on the archive where 94 per cent of this method's picks live, and its extra far purchases converted at roughly a quarter of the inherited rate (increment mass 4.752540 against 5.978073, panel -0.081702); n-82195b802723 reserved two picks per batch for the archive-far half and converted at 0.40x the near half (panel -0.031639); n-19063a19f7ec closed two waste channels at admission and still lost increment mass (panel -0.043178). n-1c27fae8e61d changed the uncertainty model itself and de-priced the incumbent's own regime (-0.136643). The one quantity left untested is the scale of the dispersion on the near field, which is where this method actually buys.

adoptions.applicability: Applies to this node because its predictor already publishes a mean and an SD per selected candidate and already receives the matching score one batch later, so the paper's prediction-outcome pairs exist here without any new construction. It does not apply as a coverage guarantee: there is no calibration split at 300 chronological accepted observations, the records are the selected stream rather than an exchangeable sample, and the measured defect on this Anchor is five times too narrow in the bulk on one objective and slightly too wide on another, so only a bounded, one-sided robust scale is claimed.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Post-hoc recalibration of an existing probabilistic regressor's dispersion from its own recorded prediction-outcome pairs, with the model and its predictive mean left untouched.

deviations.adopted_setting: One global scalar per announced batch, the median absolute standardized residual of the most recent 100 eligible accepted records divided by 0.6745, applied identically to every pool member.
deviations.paper_setting: A learned recalibration map (isotonic regression over predicted quantiles) fitted on a held-out calibration set, producing per-prediction corrected quantiles.
deviations.reason: No held-out calibration set exists inside a 300-observation session without spending the surrogate's own training data, and a per-candidate interval construction is a second untested construction on top of this one; the campaign rule is one declared change per position, and the conformal per-candidate route is the registered successor if this scalar proves too coarse.

deviations.adopted_setting: Recomputed at every announced batch on a 100-record trailing window, pinned to exactly 1.0 below 20 records and clipped one-sidedly to [1.0, 10.0] so it can only widen.
deviations.paper_setting: Calibration is applied once the model is trained, with enough data for the asymptotic guarantee, and corrects both over- and under-dispersion.
deviations.reason: The session is 29 announced batches long and its predictor is refitted every batch, so a stationary correction is not available; the lower clip keeps the inherited arithmetic bit-identical where the predictor is already honest or over-cautious, which preserves the registered median_2 margin and gives an internal control stratum, and the upper clip prevents a degenerate scale from an early session.

deviations.adopted_setting: The correction is read as an allocation heuristic: the registered endpoint evidence is what the purchases and their conversion do, with the corrected residual distribution reported first as the activation check.
deviations.paper_setting: Calibration is evaluated by interval coverage as an end in itself.
deviations.reason: This campaign has already measured that improved interval coverage alone does not buy endpoint gain on this lineage - a round-16 feedback-amplitude arm moved nominal 95 per cent coverage from 77.91 to 90.69 per cent and lost 0.038141 - so coverage is registered as an activation observable and never as the result.

adoptions.implementation_change: FingerprintPosterior gains a bounded chronological store of absolute standardized residuals filled in Evolution.observe from the already joined accepted score and provenance['posterior_prediction'] (mean, unscaled std), and a predictive_scale() method that returns median(window)/0.6745 clipped to [1.0, 10.0]; FingerprintPosterior.select multiplies the sampled residual term by that scalar, which multiplies every pool member's predictive SD by it while the predictive mean is added unchanged.

adoptions.applicability: Applies as the reason the correction targets dispersion rather than the ordering statistic, and as the reason no representation change belongs here: the Anchor already uses radius-two 2048-bin integer Morgan counts under the generalized Tanimoto kernel, which is the paper's second fix, already satisfied. Its first fix is not transferable as written - this lineage fits no marginal likelihood and already declares prior amplitude 1.0 - so what is borrowed is the diagnosis, corrected here from the predictor's own measured errors instead of from a declared constant. Its third fix, proposals per selection, is a different axis and belongs to a separate position.
adoptions.borrowed_element: The diagnosis that a Tanimoto-kernel GP in this architecture class carries a predictive scale that is too small for the data it is fitted on, and that the fix belongs in the declared dispersion rather than in the acquisition or the representation.

deviations.adopted_setting: Leave the prior amplitude at its inherited 1.0 and correct the realized predictive SD after the fact by a scalar measured from the predictor's own one-step-ahead errors in this session.
deviations.paper_setting: Fix the prior signal variance by declaring an outputscale of 1.0 instead of fitting it by marginal likelihood, before any data arrives.
deviations.reason: This lineage already declares amplitude 1.0 and fits no hyperparameters, so the paper's fix is already in place and cannot be applied again; the residual defect measured here is in the conditioned posterior on the near field, which only a data-driven post-hoc correction can reach, and a distance-gated prior-variance version of the same idea was already refuted on this Anchor at -0.081702.

deviations.adopted_setting: The inherited correlated Thompson rule, announced batches of ten, 300 accepted observations per task and final Top-1 scoring on five frozen tasks, with the acquisition rule itself untouched.
deviations.paper_setting: UCB with beta drawn log-uniformly from [0.01, 1], batch size one, a 10,000-call budget and AUC Top-10 scoring over 23 tasks.
deviations.reason: The stage profile freezes batch size, budget, tasks and scoring, and this position is defined as the arm that changes the dispersion alone so that the acquisition change can be attributed separately; no number reported in that paper is campaign evidence at this budget.

adoptions.implementation_change: The correction is confined to the dispersion the acquisition reads: FingerprintPosterior.select scales only the sampled residual, and the kernel, the count fingerprints, the normalization with its 0.001 floor, the 0.05 noise SD and the predictive mean are left exactly as inherited.

literature_review.conclusion: Reusing the ticket's frozen Search Policy review r46-bottleneck-candidate-pricing-and-ranking, whose recorded candidate method for this position is exactly 'Session-calibrated predictive scale: prior-width correction and post-hoc recalibration of the dispersion the acquisition reads', and carrying only two of its sources. The literature settles two questions and no more. Tripp and Hernandez-Lobato name the defect - a Tanimoto-kernel GP in this architecture class carries a predictive scale that is too small - and locate the fix in the declared dispersion rather than in the acquisition or the representation, whose count-fingerprint half this Anchor already satisfies. Kuleshov, Fenner and Ermon supply the principle that such a dispersion can be corrected post hoc from the model's own prediction-outcome pairs without touching the model or its mean, which is the only thing this position does. Neither supplies the estimator. Its robust median form, its 100-record window, its one-sided clip at 1.0 and its upper clip at 10.0 rest on this campaign's own measurements: the bulk and the tail of this predictor's standardized residuals disagree by an order of magnitude, the earlier squared-error estimator on an earlier Parent contracted exactly the objective this Anchor protects and lost 0.038141, and pure posterior-mean-only allocation costs 0.116317 while composite selector removal costs 0.128183, so nothing that would collapse toward either extreme is admissible. Literature origin is not permission to continue: one complete exposed panel ends this recipe, and a loss with a corrected residual distribution is recorded as the answer that the inherited under-dispersion is load-bearing, with no sweep of the statistic, window, clip or form.

sources.applicability: The prior-width half is the published statement of this lineage's own measured defect: a Tanimoto-kernel GP fitted on this architecture's early data carries a dispersion that is too small, which on this Anchor's own picks is a mean squared standardized residual of 40.72 near the archive against 6.69 far. It names the defect and licenses correcting the dispersion rather than the ordering statistic; it does not supply this estimator, since this lineage fits no kernel hyperparameters at all and its amplitude is already declared at 1.0. The count-fingerprint half is already satisfied here and is adopted as confirmation that no representation change belongs in this position.
sources.finding: Tripp and Hernandez-Lobato (ICML 2024 AI for Science workshop) diagnose three defects in the PMO GP-BO baseline and report that fixing them makes a basic GP BO the strongest entry they measure: the prior signal variance fitted by marginal likelihood on poor starting data is too small and is replaced by a declared outputscale of 1.0 for objectives in [0,1]; binary Morgan fingerprints over-smooth the Tanimoto kernel and are replaced by count fingerprints; and the acquisition was maximized over only about six proposals per selection, raised to about one thousand with batch size one. Their acquisition stays UCB with beta drawn log-uniformly from [0.01, 1]. They describe it as a pilot without ablations, so the three fixes are not separated.
sources.title: Diagnosing and fixing common problems in Bayesian optimization for molecule design

sources.applicability: Supplies the principle for the one declared change: correct the dispersion of an existing predictive distribution from the model's own recorded prediction-outcome pairs, leaving the model, its kernel and its mean untouched. It applies here because this Anchor already logs exactly the pairs the principle needs - the predictive mean and SD published for each candidate in the batch it was selected, joined to the score the oracle returned - so the correction needs no new model, no new data and no new dependency. The adaptation is severe and is pre-registered as such: no held-out calibration set exists at 300 chronological accepted observations, so no distributional guarantee is claimed and the correction is a single bounded robust scale.
sources.finding: Kuleshov, Fenner and Ermon (ICML 2018) recalibrate a probabilistic regressor post hoc, by a procedure inspired by Platt scaling, and report that it is guaranteed to produce calibrated uncertainty estimates given enough data while consistently producing well-calibrated credible intervals for Bayesian linear regression and for feedforward and recurrent networks.
sources.title: Accurate Uncertainties for Deep Learning Using Calibrated Regression

hypothesis: Session-calibrated robust predictive scale on the dispersion the allocation rule reads. At each announced batch the selector forms one scalar from the inherited posterior's own one-step-ahead records for this session's accepted candidates - for each accepted molecule, the predictive mean and the unscaled predictive SD logged in the batch it was selected, against its observed score - by taking the median absolute standardized residual over the most recent 100 such records, dividing by 0.6745 to convert it to a Gaussian-equivalent dispersion, and clipping the result to [1.0, 10.0]; fewer than 20 records leaves the scalar at exactly 1.0. Every pool member's predictive SD is multiplied by that one scalar before the acquisition reads it, which in this correlated Thompson rule means the sampled residual term is multiplied by the scalar while the predictive mean is added unchanged. The scalar is global over the pool and is always computed from the inherited unscaled SD, never from an already corrected one, so it measures the inherited predictor and cannot close a feedback loop on itself. The predictive mean, the kernel, the normalization and its 0.001 floor, the 0.05 noise SD, the Cholesky jitter ladder, the cross-candidate covariance and its factor, the ten standard-normal rows and their consumption order, the stall-time eligibility mask and its K=3 counter, the per-pick mask update and the first-index tie rule are all exactly as inherited, and a scalar of exactly 1.0 takes the inherited arithmetic path unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Honest dispersion activated exactly as registered and cost chemistry: increments 5.978 to 5.451, panel -0.0352, every seed down
finding_summary.insights: The question the ticket asked is answered in the first of its two registered directions: the inherited near-archive over-confidence of this predictor is load-bearing. Giving the correlated Thompson rule a dispersion that matches its own measured errors does change what it buys - in the registered direction, measured inside the same batches on the same draws - and what it buys is worse. That ends the scale hypothesis on this Anchor, with no sweep of the statistic, the window, the clip bounds or the form, which is exactly what the intent pre-registered a loss to mean. It also settles the older ambiguity: the round-16 scaled-residual arm and the two constant-amplitude arms all lost, and it was never clear whether their estimators or the idea itself were at fault; a median-based, one-sided, exactly reproducible estimator that leaves four cells byte-identical loses too, so the object, not the estimator, is what the method cannot absorb. The mechanism of the loss is the useful part, and it is specific to how uncertainty and chemistry line up in this representation. Under an accepted-only count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto GP, predictive SD is largest exactly where kernel similarity to the archive is smallest, and in a graph generator the members furthest from the archive are not novel scaffolds but degenerate fragments - a bare halogen, a two-atom molecule. So widening the sampled residual does not buy exploration, it buys mass loss: the swapped-in picks are five heavy atoms smaller on average, one in seven of them is a five-atom-or-smaller fragment, and the molecular reading of the same cells shows the widened sessions shrinking (26.8 to 20.8 mean heavy atoms on the worst cell, one- and two-atom proposals still being made after evaluation 200 at 21 of 790 picks in widened batches against 3 of 710 in unit batches) while the unchanged cells carry the cleanest chemistry in the run. Dispersion in this method cannot distinguish novelty from degeneracy, so any method that spends variance through this surrogate will spend it on fragments. A second finding worth carrying: on-policy calibration improved while the score fell. The Child's own raw residuals are better behaved than the Anchor's (pooled median absolute 0.6685 against 0.7156, sitagliptin_mpo 2.2931 against 3.3339), and the multiplier's realised tail collapsed against its offline forecast, because an allocation that buys high-variance candidates makes its own predictions look honest. Calibration measured on a policy's own purchases is therefore not a proxy for allocation quality in this campaign, and no future arm should treat a falling standardised residual as evidence of progress. On the method itself, the trajectories say the limit is not the width of the uncertainty but the shape of the search. Purchases stay on top of the archive - 76.8 per cent of all 4,350 picks sit at kernel similarity 0.8 or above to the accepted set, and mean similarity rises from 0.794 in the first half of a session to 0.856 in the second - so the late search is sustained local refinement of a handful of inherited scaffolds, which the molecular report sees as best-of-cell clusters that differ only in which halogen occupies which position. The one exploration lever this method has is the sampled residual, and this node has now measured that the lever is confounded with molecular size, so turning it harder is not available. The miscalibration that remains is also the wrong kind for a width fix: on sitagliptin_mpo the residuals are asymmetric, with a third of picks more than three SDs below prediction and mean square still 111 after correction, which is a bias in the predictive mean, not a width defect. What could remove the limitation is a different class of component, not a different constant: a criterion that prices improvement over the session's incumbent rather than a raw sampled value, so that a high-variance near-floor fragment is never competitive; a surrogate or ranking model whose uncertainty is conditioned on something other than kernel distance, so that distance-from-archive stops being a synonym for smallness; or a proposal operator set with fragment-level moves and a size floor, so that the variance the search does spend lands on different chemistry rather than on fewer atoms. The first of those is already bound this round as a separate position, and this node is its attribution control: the identical scale construction costs 0.527 of increment mass on its own, so any gain that arm shows is attributable to the improvement-priced criterion and not to the scale underneath it. What stays open is whether the same correction behaves differently under a criterion that cannot be fooled by a fragment, and whether the near-archive mean bias - the part a robust scale deliberately ignores - is itself worth a separate intervention. Two borrowed elements were on trial here and both behaved: the published post-hoc recalibration of a probabilistic regressor's dispersion from its own prediction-outcome pairs ran exactly as borrowed, reproducible at every announcement, and the published diagnosis that a Tanimoto-kernel Gaussian process of this architecture class is under-dispersed was confirmed on this Anchor's own records before anything changed. What did not transfer is the inference that fixing it helps, and the deviations say how far that counterexample reaches: a single bulk scalar replaces a fitted quantile map, the clip is one-sided so contraction was never tested, and the correction sits under a correlated ten-position batch draw rather than the single-point acquisition the sources studied. The campaign can record that an honest dispersion is not a benefit in this architecture at this budget, not that calibration is worthless. As a continuation this position also did what it promised: it differs from the round-16 scaled-residual arm in estimator, in being unable to contract, and in protecting the four cells where that arm's largest losses fell, and all three held - so the repeated loss is attributable to the object rather than to the estimator, and the registered rule that a loss ends the scale hypothesis on this Anchor with no sweep applies. The route stops; the remaining iteration worth having is not another scale but a criterion or surrogate class that changes what high variance can buy.
finding_summary.results: The correction fired and every pre-registered intermediate number landed where it was forecast. The per-batch scalar was reproducible to float equality from the session's own accepted prediction-outcome records in all 435 announcements, with zero records excluded anywhere: exactly 1.0 at 195 announcements (forecast 202), above 1.0 at 240 (forecast 233), at or above 2 at 124 (forecast 126), median 1.1323 (forecast 1.1296). The heavy upper tail did not materialise - at or above 5 at only 7 announcements against a forecast 52, the upper clip of 10 never reached, realised maximum 9.3626, mean 1.7702 against a forecast 2.2171 - because the widened rule buys candidates the predictor is less wrong about, so the miscalibration it measures on its own picks shrinks as it acts. Exposure was exactly as heterogeneous as registered without any task identity being read: median_2 stayed at exactly 1.0 in all 87 of its announcements, deco_hop ran 1.0-1.47, zaleplon_mpo 1.0-1.95, drd2_docking 1.0-3.87 and sitagliptin_mpo up to 9.36. The dispersion it was meant to fix did fall toward one: pooled median absolute standardised residual 0.6685 to 0.4844 (Gaussian-equivalent 0.9911 to 0.7181; the Anchor's own records sit at 0.7156 and 1.0609), sitagliptin_mpo 2.2931 to 0.6578, drd2_docking 0.8916 to 0.5478, zaleplon_mpo 0.8204 to 0.6598, deco_hop 0.5013 to 0.4774, median_2 untouched at 0.2573; on the 2,400 picks made in widened batches, 1.1050 to 0.5852 with mean square 14.91 to 1.67. As registered, the asymmetric lower tail survived: sitagliptin_mpo mean square moved only 136.73 to 111.28, against a forecast 143.5 to 110.8. The allocation moved exactly where the scalar moved and nowhere else. The unit-scale replay on identical pools returned ten of ten picks in 195 of 195 exactly-one batches and fewer than ten in 218 of 240 widened batches (mean ordered overlap 5.08, 953 picks displaced and 953 swapped in). Purchases at posterior-mean rank 40 or worse rose to 48.03 per cent in widened unrestricted batches against 41.21 per cent in exactly-one batches of the same runs and 28.73 per cent on the Anchor, mean posterior-SD rank fell 84.40 to 67.23, and archive-far purchases (kernel similarity below 0.5) rose from 3.39 to 12.47 per cent. The mask-restricted stratum kept 0 of 830 picks at rank 40 or worse, as it must. Everything else held: every pool 160 members, a (10, 160) normal array per batch at unchanged consumption, the logged scaled SD equal to the inherited SD times the logged scalar in 435 of 435 pools with zero relative error, the jitter ladder at 1e-8 with no failed fit and no fallback anywhere, the mask size rule and the K=3 counter agreeing with an independent recount in 435 of 435 batches, and the far-to-near predictive SD ratio at 1.7343 in the cells that reproduce the Anchor against the inherited 1.7477. Five of fifteen sessions came out bit-identical to the Anchor for all 300 evaluations - median_2 on all three seeds, deco_hop seed 0 as forecast, and deco_hop seed 1, whose single widened batch happened to pick the same ten molecules - and the first two announcements of all fifteen sessions reproduced the Anchor evaluation for evaluation. What the honest width bought was worse chemistry. Within the same batches, on the same pools and the same draws, the picks the inherited rule would have made average 26.40 heavy atoms and the picks that replaced them 21.79, with 142 of the 953 swapped-in picks at five heavy atoms or fewer against none of the 953 displaced; at each session's first diverging batch, where the pool is still the Anchor's own, displaced picks average 29.35 heavy atoms and their replacements 19.24. Those replacements scored 0.1886 on average against 0.3839 for the picks both rules agreed on in the same widened batches (drd2_docking 0.333 against 0.635, sitagliptin_mpo 0.086 against 0.154), and they converted at 0.001608 of incumbent increment per evaluation against 0.002245 for the agreed picks, about 0.72 times the rate. Whole-run realised increment mass fell to 5.450779 over 229 improvements from the Anchor's 5.978073 over 253, parent-beating offspring fell from 14.57 to 13.79 per cent and the mean accepted score from 0.3782 to 0.3353. The panel came out 0.571877 against 0.607030, a paired delta of -0.035153 with all three seeds down (-0.062302, -0.022834, -0.020323). That figure sits inside this Anchor's own law-free band [-0.055482, +0.014579], so the panel mean alone cannot separate this arm from path luck; the cell level can, because the loss is concentrated where the intervention is: sitagliptin_mpo fell on all three seeds (-0.289855, -0.153239, -0.085629) while the law-free re-draw moved that same cell -0.095612, +0.012912, +0.038270, and the four protected median_2 and deco_hop seed-0 cells are exactly zero because they never left scalar 1.0.

It also settles the older ambiguity: the round-16 scaled-residual arm and the two constant-amplitude arms all lost, and it was never clear whether their estimators or the idea itself were at fault; a median-based, one-sided, exactly reproducible estimator that leaves four cells byte-identical loses too, so the object, not the estimator, is what the method cannot absorb. The mechanism of the loss is the useful part, and it is specific to how uncertainty and chemistry line up in this representation. Under an accepted-only count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto GP, predictive SD is largest exactly where kernel similarity to the archive is smallest, and in a graph generator the members furthest from the archive are not novel scaffolds but degenerate fragments - a bare halogen, a two-atom molecule. So widening the sampled residual does not buy exploration, it buys mass loss: the swapped-in picks are five heavy atoms smaller on average, one in seven of them is a five-atom-or-smaller fragment, and the molecular reading of the same cells shows the widened sessions shrinking (26.8 to 20.8 mean heavy atoms on the worst cell, one- and two-atom proposals still being made after evaluation 200 at 21 of 790 picks in widened batches against 3 of 710 in unit batches) while the unchanged cells carry the cleanest chemistry in the run. Dispersion in this method cannot distinguish novelty from degeneracy, so any method that spends variance through this surrogate will spend it on fragments. A second finding worth carrying: on-policy calibration improved while the score fell. The Child's own raw residuals are better behaved than the Anchor's (pooled median absolute 0.6685 against 0.7156, sitagliptin_mpo 2.2931 against 3.3339), and the multiplier's realised tail collapsed against its offline forecast, because an allocation that buys high-variance candidates makes its own predictions look honest. Calibration measured on a policy's own purchases is therefore not a proxy for allocation quality in this campaign, and no future arm should treat a falling standardised residual as evidence of progress. On the method itself, the trajectories say the limit is not the width of the uncertainty but the shape of the search. Purchases stay on top of the archive - 76.8 per cent of all 4,350 picks sit at kernel similarity 0.8 or above to the accepted set, and mean similarity rises from 0.794 in the first half of a session to 0.856 in the second - so the late search is sustained local refinement of a handful of inherited scaffolds, which the molecular report sees as best-of-cell clusters that differ only in which halogen occupies which position. The one exploration lever this method has is the sampled residual, and this node has now measured that the lever is confounded with molecular size, so turning it harder is not available. The miscalibration that remains is also the wrong kind for a width fix: on sitagliptin_mpo the residuals are asymmetric, with a third of picks more than three SDs below prediction and mean square still 111 after correction, which is a bias in the predictive mean, not a width defect. What could remove the limitation is a different class of component, not a different constant: a criterion that prices improvement over the session's incumbent rather than a raw sampled value, so that a high-variance near-floor fragment is never competitive; a surrogate or ranking model whose uncertainty is conditioned on something other than kernel distance, so that distance-from-archive stops being a synonym for smallness; or a proposal operator set with fragment-level moves and a size floor, so that the variance the search does spend lands on different chemistry rather than on fewer atoms. The first of those is already bound this round as a separate position, and this node is its attribution control: the identical scale construction costs 0.527 of increment mass on its own, so any gain that arm shows is attributable to the improvement-priced criterion and not to the scale underneath it. What stays open is whether the same correction behaves differently under a criterion that cannot be fooled by a fragment, and whether the near-archive mean bias - the part a robust scale deliberately ignores - is itself worth a separate intervention. Two borrowed elements were on trial here and both behaved: the published post-hoc recalibration of a probabilistic regressor's dispersion from its own prediction-outcome pairs ran exactly as borrowed, reproducible at every announcement, and the published diagnosis that a Tanimoto-kernel Gaussian process of this architecture class is under-dispersed was confirmed on this Anchor's own records before anything changed. What did not transfer is the inference that fixing it helps, and the deviations say how far that counterexample reaches: a single bulk scalar replaces a fitted quantile map, the clip is one-sided so contraction was never tested, and the correction sits under a correlated ten-position batch draw rather than the single-point acquisition the sources studied. The campaign can record that an honest dispersion is not a benefit in this architecture at this budget, not that calibration is worthless. As a continuation this position also did what it promised: it differs from the round-16 scaled-residual arm in estimator, in being unable to contract, and in protecting the four cells where that arm's largest losses fell, and all three held - so the repeated loss is attributable to the object rather than to the estimator, and the registered rule that a loss ends the scale hypothesis on this Anchor with no sweep applies. The route stops; the remaining iteration worth having is not another scale but a criterion or surrogate class that changes what high variance can buy.

molecular.headline: Ring-dense, halogen-painted heteroaromatics with zero stereochemistry; the widened cells shrank to fragments.
molecular.overall_character: Across 4350 optimizer proposals the node emits medium-sized, heavily cyclised heteroaromatics: mean SMILES length 42-57 characters, mean 22.5-31.7 heavy atoms, ring_closure_rate 0.89-0.99 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.80-0.98 in every cell. The frameworks are recognisable medicinal-chemistry cores (indoles, quinolines, xanthines, benzoxazoles, quinazolines, fused diketopiperazines, benzoquinolizidines) decorated almost exclusively by single atoms: methyl, methoxy, amino, and above all halogen (halogen_rate 0.82-0.97 on four of five cells). The decoration is where the chemistry breaks down. 943 of 4350 proposals (22%) carry at least one nitrogen-halogen bond, 368 (8.5%) an oxygen-halogen bond, 90 a sulfur-halogen bond, and those motifs sit in the highest-scoring molecules of three cells, not only in the discarded tail. Meanwhile not one proposal in 4350 contains a trifluoromethyl group, not one carries a stereocentre (stereocentre_rate 0.0 in every cell), and not one carries a formal charge (charged_rate 0.0). Within a cell the late search is a one-scaffold neighbourhood: the twelve best molecules of one cell are eight copies of the same indole-2-carboxamide differing only in which halogen sits on the amide nitrogen and on the ring nitrogen. Three of the five cells (and two individual sessions in a fourth) ran with the sampled term widened relative to the Anchor: in those sessions the proposals are measurably smaller, 26/290, 22/290 and 29/290 molecules at five heavy atoms or fewer against 8/290, 3/290 and 6/290 in the same seeds of the Anchor, with mean heavy-atom count falling from 26.8 to 20.8 on the worst-affected seed. The two cells that ran unchanged are byte-identical to the Anchor's own trajectories, 300/300 proposals, and carry the cleanest chemistry in the run.

per_task.generated_character: Roughly 24 heavy atoms per molecule (mean SMILES length 43, max 79), overwhelmingly a methyl/methoxy/ethyl substituted bicyclic azaindole or indole carrying one exocyclic aryl carboxamide. Seeds 1 and 2 keep that anilide: CCc1c(OC)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(F)c3cccnc3)n2Cl)c1C is the 0.4828 cluster and eight of the twelve best molecules are the same skeleton with F, Cl or Br permuted on the amide N and on the pyrrole N. Seed 0 is a different cell: after roughly evaluation 190 it folds the amide nitrogen into the ring system and proposes strained fused tetracyclics with aminal N-CH-N centres and cyclobutane fusions, e.g. its final and best molecule COCC1c2c(C)c(C)c3cc4oc3c2N(c2ccc(F)nc2)C41 at 0.3883 and the furo-fused indoline COc1c(C)c2c3c4oc(cc14)C(C2CN)N3c1ccc(F)cc1 at 0.3763. In that cell only 14 of the 150 proposals after evaluation 150 still contain any C(=O)N or C(=S)N linkage, against 125 and 127 in the other two seeds; the acyclic carboxamide was consumed into rings and never rebuilt. Aminomethyl (CN) and thiomethyl (CS) appendages replace it.
liabilities: N-halogenated amides in eight of the twelve best molecules; N-F and N-Br amides are oxidants, not products
halogen on the pyrrole-type ring nitrogen (n2Cl, n2Br, n2F), which is not an isolable substitution
433 of 870 proposals (50%) carry at least one nitrogen-halogen bond
the seed 0 cell builds aminal and strained four-membered-ring fusions such as C41 closures that no route would deliver
late-run degenerate fragments (FS at evaluation 259) waste oracle calls
missing_features: a tertiary amide whose nitrogen carries a carbon substituent (N-ethyl or N-acetyl) rather than a halogen
an aryl nitrile; nitriles appear 252 times elsewhere in the run but in none of the twelve best molecules here
a fused pyrazolo- or imidazo-pyrimidine bicycle alongside the retained carboxamide
any stereocentre at all; stereocentre_rate is 0.0 over all 870 proposals
acyclic flexible linkers of two or more sp3 carbons between the two ring systems
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rises with a planar methoxy/methyl-decorated bicyclic heteroaromatic bearing an intact exocyclic C(=O)N-aryl, with a 3-pyridyl cap scoring above phenyl (0.4828 for N-c3cccnc3 versus 0.3727 for the phenyl analogue COc1c(C)c2c3c4oc(cc14)C(C2CN)N3c1ccccc1). It is indifferent to what sits on the amide nitrogen: N-F, N-Cl and N-Br analogues all return the identical 0.4828. Scores collapse to 0.0 for stripped fragments such as FS, ClBr and BrBr, still proposed as late as evaluation 259, and fall by about 0.1 wherever the amide is cyclised away.

per_task.generated_character: The largest molecules in the run, mean SMILES length 57 and max 191, 31.7 heavy atoms on average, ring_closure_rate 0.969. Every seed converges on a biaryl-type pairing of two fused heteroaromatic systems. Seed 0, which ran identically to the Anchor, builds a pyrazolo-fused purine-2-thione N-linked to a chloro-quinazolin-4-yl: O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3 at 0.8561. Seed 1 builds a pyrimido-oxazinone bearing an aryl ether to a dichloro-cyanopyridine: C=C(F)c1c(Oc2cccc(-c3ncc(C#N)c(Cl)c3Cl)c2)nc2oc(=O)nc(SBr)c2c1CC#N at 0.6217. Seed 2, which diverged from the Anchor at evaluation 31, builds a benzoxazole bearing a difluoromethylamino-fluoropyrimidine, FOc1c(F)c(C(F)(F)Nc2ncc(F)c(F)n2)c2ocnc2c1Br at 0.6296. Decoration is almost entirely halogen; only 2% of proposals carry an amide and only 3% an aliphatic ring nitrogen.
liabilities: 275 of 870 proposals (32%) contain an O-halogen bond; the aryl hypofluorite OF sits in every one of the best molecules
alpha-halo ethers such as C(F)OCCl, which are alkylating agents rather than stable substituents
a sulfenyl bromide SBr in the top seed 1 cluster
cumulated dienes such as C=C=C(F) in the seed 2 cluster, reported as cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.0644
thiocarbonyl c(=S) cores that would tautomerise or oxidise readily
missing_features: a sulfonamide or sulfone linker; S(=O)(=O) appears in no proposal for this objective
a basic aliphatic amine on the periphery; only 3% of proposals carry an aliphatic ring nitrogen
a flexible aliphatic linker of three or more sp3 atoms between the two ring systems
a genuine trifluoromethyl or difluoromethyl aryl substituent built on carbon rather than on oxygen
an exocyclic carboxamide, present in only 2% of the 870 proposals
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Everything that keeps no recognisable scaffold sits at exactly 0.5000, including C=C, CBr, NCCCl and C#CF, so the gradient above the floor is entirely about assembling and holding a two-ring-system framework linked by a direct bond or a short ether. Within that framework the score moves by hundredths for halogen swaps (0.8561 for -c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45 against 0.8561 for the CCl homologue) and drops when a ring is opened or a fusion is broken (0.8561 to 0.7989 for the ring-opened O=C1C2=C3CN... variant).

per_task.generated_character: Mean 27.6 heavy atoms, ring_closure_rate 0.93, halogen_rate 0.969. The high-scoring molecules are lipophilic fused polycyclics carrying one aliphatic ring nitrogen and one pendant meta-substituted phenyl. Seed 0 settles on a benzoquinolizidine with a 3-aminophenyl and ring fluorine, CC1CN2CCC(c3cccc(NCl)c3)CC2c2cc(N)cc(F)c21 at 0.9913, and on methylthio-bearing homologues such as CSCC(CC1CCN2CC(C)c3c(F)cc(N)cc3C2C1)c1cccc(NCl)c1 at 0.9937. Seed 1 settles on a spiro aminal, a 3-chlorophenyl on a quaternary carbon bridging an azetidine-fused diamine, CCCCCc1c(OC)c2cc(Cl)c1C1(c3cccc(Cl)c3)N3CCC3(C)N21 at 0.9950. Seed 2 settles on a tetracyclic carbazole-like framework with a quaternary carbon bearing 3-fluoro-5-(1-fluoroethyl)phenyl, COc1c2[nH]c3c4ccc(c13)C(c1cc(F)cc(C(C)F)c1)(CCC4)CC2 at 0.9822. Aliphatic ring nitrogen is present in 43% of all 870 proposals and in 33 of the 60 per-seed top-20 molecules, so the basic centre is genuinely there.
liabilities: N-chloroanilines (NCl) in most of the seed 0 top molecules; 175 of 870 proposals carry a nitrogen-halogen bond
azetidine-fused aminal spiro centres such as N3CCC3(C)N21, which are strained aminals, not stable amines
20 of 290 proposals in seed 0 and 21 of 290 in seed 2 are five heavy atoms or fewer, against 3 and 7 in the Anchor's matched seeds
benzylic C(C)F fluorides that would solvolyse
missing_features: an acyclic three- or four-carbon chain linking the aryl group to the basic nitrogen
an explicitly ionisable or quaternised nitrogen; charged_rate is 0.0 over all proposals
stereochemistry on the ring-fusion and quaternary carbons, which are drawn flat in all 870 proposals
a trifluoromethyl aryl substituent, absent from every proposal in the run
an amide or sulfonamide retained as part of a high-scoring molecule rather than discarded early
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient runs from the sulfonamides and carboxylic acids of the seed pool, COS(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 at 0.0002 and O=C(NCl)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 at 0.0002, up to lipophilic polycycles with an embedded aliphatic nitrogen and a halogenated pendant aryl near 0.99. It rewards removing polar sulfonyl and acid groups, adding ring fusions, and keeping a meta-substituted phenyl on a quaternary or benzylic carbon; it is nearly flat between F, Cl and NH2 on the fused arene (0.9913, 0.9913, 0.9901).

per_task.generated_character: The cleanest and most drug-like chemistry in the run, and the only cell whose three sessions reproduce the Anchor's trajectories exactly, 300 of 300 proposals per seed. Mean 30.3 heavy atoms, ring_closure_rate 0.986, halogen_rate only 0.101, amide present in 60% of proposals and an aliphatic ring nitrogen in 69%. The converged motif is a 2-alkyl or 2-alkoxy quinolin-4-yl attached to a fused bicyclic 2,5-diketopiperazine: CCCc1cc(N2C3CC4=C(NCN4C(=O)CN(C)C3=O)C2CC)c2ccccc2n1 at 0.2424. Seed 1 reaches the same chemistry through an N-linked pyrazole, CCOc1cc(-n2nc3c(c2CC)CC(=O)N(C)C(=O)CN3C)c2ccccc2n1 at 0.2213; seed 0 through a dibenzoxepine-fused variant, CCCN1CN(C)CC(=O)C2=C3c4cc5ccc4Oc4ccc(OCC)c(C)c4C5N3C2CN1 at 0.2228.
liabilities: aminal N-CH-N centres inside the fused ring (NCN4), which hydrolyse
partially saturated, tautomer-ambiguous rings drawn as C3=C4 with sp3 fusion carbons
11 of 870 proposals are five heavy atoms or fewer, including bare C at evaluation 281
ethyl and propyl groups added purely as score filler on an already saturated motif
missing_features: a methylenedioxyphenyl or other fused benzodioxole ring attached to the diketopiperazine
an indole fused into the diketopiperazine rather than a quinoline hung off its nitrogen
a sulfonamide-linked piperazine tail; no proposal in this cell contains S(=O)(=O)
stereochemistry on the two ring-fusion carbons of the diketopiperazine, which are flat in all 870 proposals
a pyrazolo-pyrimidinone core as an alternative to the diketopiperazine
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The whole cell lives in a band of 0.19 to 0.24: the median proposal is 0.192 and the best 0.2424, so the search is polishing one hybrid motif rather than moving. Score drops when the diketopiperazine carbonyl becomes a thiocarbonyl (0.2424 to 0.2193 for the C(=S) analogue) and when the bicyclic fusion is opened to an acyclic anilino chain (0.2217). Single-atom proposals such as C, C=C and C#C score 0.0 and were still being made at evaluation 281.

per_task.generated_character: The smallest and least cyclised molecules in the run: mean 22.5 heavy atoms, mean SMILES length 42.2, ring_closure_rate 0.889 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.799, both the lowest of the five cells, with 77 of 870 proposals at five heavy atoms or fewer and 97 fully acyclic. The recurring framework is a xanthine or purine-2,6-dione: seed 2 reaches 0.5345 with Cc1c2c(c(CF)n1C=CC(=CC=CO)NF)c(=O)n(F)c(=O)n2C, a dimethyl xanthine carrying a fluoromethyl and a conjugated enol-polyene tail; seed 1 reaches 0.4911 with Cn1c(=O)c2c3n(C4(F)C(O)=CC=C4F)c(c2n(C)c1=O)C(OC=CF)C3, a xanthine fused to a fluorinated cyclopentenol; seed 0 reaches 0.4760 with CC=C(O)C(=CC)C1=CNC2=C(N(CF)C1)N(C=O)C(=O)C2(F)F, in which the aromatic core has been reduced to a dihydropyrimidinone with a gem-difluoro carbon and an open polyene enol chain. Fluorine is present everywhere but always as isolated C-F, N-F or CH2F; the cell contains no CF3 at all.
liabilities: 273 of 870 proposals (31%) carry a nitrogen-halogen bond, including N-F on the xanthine imide nitrogen in the best molecule
open polyene enol chains such as CC=C(O)C(=CC) that are tautomer-unstable and would not survive isolation
N-fluoro enamine fragments (NF on C=CC(=CC=CO)) that are reagents rather than molecules
the heaviest fragment waste in the run: 26, 22 and 29 of 290 proposals at five heavy atoms or fewer per seed, against 8, 3 and 6 in the Anchor's matched seeds
a formyl group on ring nitrogen (N(C=O)) used as filler
missing_features: a trifluoromethyl group; the gradient rewards fluorine yet not one proposal in the entire run contains CF3
a polyfluorinated aryl ring such as a di- or trifluorophenyl carrying all its fluorine on carbon
a primary aliphatic amine beta to a carbonyl, i.e. a free beta-amino amide fragment
a saturated fused diazabicycle carrying the fluorinated substituent, instead of a flat xanthine
stereochemistry; this is the cell where configuration matters most and stereocentre_rate is 0.0
a gem-difluoro or trifluoro carbon built deliberately; only 39 proposals in 4350 contain any C(F)(F) centre
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score climbs steeply with fluorine count on an intact small bicyclic core and with a nitrogen-rich fused system: the median proposal is 0.0289 while the best is 0.5345, the widest span in the run, and the worst are bare F, O and C#C at 0.0. Within the converged family each additional fluorine or fluoromethyl adds hundredths (0.4558 to 0.4589 to 0.4745 across CC3F, CC3CF and the CCF homologue). Nothing in the gradient distinguishes an N-F bond from a C-F bond, so the search spends its fluorine on nitrogen.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 943 of 4350 proposals carry at least one nitrogen-halogen bond and 368 carry an oxygen-halogen bond; the motif is not confined to the discarded tail but sits in the top-scoring molecule of three of the five objective cells, for instance an N-fluoro aryl amide, a ring-nitrogen chloride and an aryl hypofluorite that all appear in best-of-cell molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator attaches halogens to heteroatoms as freely as to carbon, producing N-F, N-Cl, N-Br, O-F and S-Br bonds that no synthesis delivers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The substitution operator should be typed by the atom it edits: halogen substitution restricted to carbon, with heteroatom-halogen products either filtered before the oracle call or generated only where an explicit rule allows it. This costs nothing in diversity and removes the single largest source of unmakeable proposals.

transferable_gaps.evidence: stereocentre_rate is 0.0 in all five cells and no '@' character appears in any of the 4350 optimizer proposals, even though the converged scaffolds carry sp3 ring-fusion carbons and quaternary centres that are genuinely stereogenic, such as fused diketopiperazine fusions and quaternary aryl-bearing carbons in the polycyclic clusters.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot express stereochemistry. It has never once emitted a defined stereocentre or double-bond geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A generator whose string grammar omits stereo tokens is blind to any reward surface that separates configurational isomers; it can only ever reach the best achiral or racemic-average member of a family. Adding stereo tokens to the mutation alphabet, or a post-hoc enumeration of configurations around sp3 centres already present, opens a dimension the search currently cannot enter.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 0 of 4350 proposals contain a CF3 fragment and only 39 contain any C(F)(F) centre, while halogen_rate is 0.82 to 0.97 in four of five cells and one cell's score climbs monotonically with fluorine count up to six isolated fluorines. The generator adds fluorine one atom at a time to whichever atom is adjacent, never to the same carbon twice.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never builds polyhalogenated carbon groups: no trifluoromethyl in the entire run and almost no gem-difluoro carbon.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Single-atom substitution cannot assemble a multiply substituted carbon in one move, and intermediate singly and doubly substituted carbons may not be rewarded, so the move is never taken. The operator set needs whole-group substitution, with common chemotype fragments such as trifluoromethyl, difluoromethyl and sulfonyl inserted as units rather than reached atom by atom.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In one of fifteen sessions the search folded an exocyclic aryl carboxamide into fused polycyclics near evaluation 190; only 14 of the 150 proposals after evaluation 150 still contained any C(=O)N or C(=S)N linkage, whereas the five comparable sessions on the same chemistry retained it in 125 to 135 of 150. The affected session finished roughly 0.09 below its own matched baseline session and below the other two sessions of the same cell.
transferable_gaps.gap: Once the generator fuses an exocyclic linker into a ring, it cannot reopen it, so a session can irreversibly lose the pharmacophoric linker it started from.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The move set is biased toward ring formation with no inverse. A ring-opening or linker-restoring move, or an archive that can re-seed from an earlier non-fused elite when the current population's functional-group inventory collapses, would make that trap recoverable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the sessions that ran with a widened sampled term, 26, 22, 29, 20 and 21 of 290 proposals were five heavy atoms or fewer, against 8, 3, 6, 3 and 7 in the matched baseline sessions on the same seeds, and mean heavy-atom count fell from 26.8 to 20.8 on the worst-affected session. Fragments such as a bare fluorine, a bare oxygen, acetylene, bromomethane and chlorine-bromide were proposed as late as evaluation 259 and all scored at or near the floor.
transferable_gaps.gap: When the proposal distribution is widened, the generator loses molecular mass instead of exploring, degrading candidates to one- to five-atom fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Widening is being spent on deletion moves that shrink the molecule rather than on substitution moves that diversify it. A size-aware proposal distribution, a floor on heavy-atom count, or widening applied only to substitution and ring-addition operators would convert the extra variance into chemistry instead of into wasted oracle calls.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cumulated double-bond rate is 0.087 and 0.064 in two cells; converged elites include allene fragments, exocyclic C=N imines, aminal N-CH-N centres inside fused rings, and partially saturated rings written with sp3 fusion carbons where an aromatic ring was present a few evaluations earlier. These appear in best-of-cell molecules, not only in the tail.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator edits ring atoms without preserving aromaticity or tautomeric sense, emitting dearomatised, cumulated and aminal ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A generator that mutates ring atoms as free characters will drift out of a valid aromatic system and into strained or tautomer-ambiguous forms that are formally valid SMILES. Ring edits should be constrained to preserve the aromatic perception of the ring being edited, or be followed by a sanitisation and rejection step before the oracle is called.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No proposal in 4350 contains a tert-butyl group, a nitro group or a formal charge; sulfonyl appears only where it was inherited from the seed pool and is discarded immediately; whole best-of-cell clusters differ only in which halogen occupies one position, for instance eight molecules sharing one score to ten decimal places while F, Cl and Br permute across two sites, and late-run proposals within a session show rising character-level self-similarity (0.38 to 0.65 in one session).
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator's decoration vocabulary is one-atom wide: methyl, methoxy, amino, halogen, and almost nothing else.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Scoring plateaus are being explored with moves too small to leave them, so the search polishes one scaffold instead of jumping. A fragment-level move set and a diversity term that prices a proposal against the current elite set would broaden decoration and prevent the late-run collapse onto a single substitution pattern.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

method_references.title: Austin Tripp and José Miguel Hernández-Lobato. Genetic algorithms are strong baselines for molecule generation. arXiv:2310.09267, 2023. Sections 2–3 and Appendix A describe the anchor.

branches: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
retained_mechanisms: Task-local accepted-only chronological archive; greedy-64 score/serial survivors; score-quantile parent sampling (edges 0.1/0.25/0.5, weights 0.6/0.3/0.1); bounded fresh-pool refill at pool_multiplier 16, i.e. 160 admitted candidates per announced batch of ten (pool size 160 in all 435 batches).

All seven graph mutation operator families at unchanged weights; connected-fragment crossover at 0.45 with its optional finishing mutation; ordinary mutation continuation; disabled direct aromatic C/N exchange.

Maximum-per-signature sulfur admission over the original scored generating parents (m-93cd9a000278) and the stable canonical/isomeric identity admission path (m-213e85380e04) with both duplicate scopes: zero duplicate and zero invalid attempts in all fifteen cells.

Accepted-only chronological radius-two chirality-aware 2048-bin integer Morgan-count GP with generalized Tanimoto kernel (m-000000000003), adaptive mean and population-SD normalization with the 0.001 floor, noise SD 0.05, float64 covariance and Cholesky with the inherited jitter ladder: 435 of 435 fits ok, jitter 1e-8 throughout, no posterior fallback.

Correlated Thompson fresh-pool allocation (m-000000000005 with m-000000000006 sampled residual influence and m-000000000007 cross-candidate correlation): one (10, 160) standard-normal array per batch at unchanged shape, order and consumption count, unchanged score_scale, sequential availability-mask updates, first-index ties and the unchanged numerical-fallback path.
